claims: The Artemis II mission concluded on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission had a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego.
The Artemis II splashdown occurred at 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
The Artemis II splashdown occurred on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The crew of the Artemis II mission was Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew returned after a 10-day lunar flyby.
Recovery teams from the USS John P. Murtha assisted with the Artemis II recovery.
Jeremy Hansen is the first Canadian to travel to the Moon.
The Artemis II recovery team included NASA's Exploration Ground Systems and U.S. Navy personnel aboard the USS John P. Murtha.
The Orion capsule had a high-speed re-entry during Artemis II.
Artemis II marks the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
The Artemis II crew was extracted from the capsule after splashdown.
The Artemis II crew was taken to the USS John P. Murtha for immediate medical evaluations.
The Artemis II mission tested the heat shield.
The Artemis II mission tested overall spacecraft performance.
The Artemis II crew completed a high-speed entry.
The Artemis II high-speed entry tested the spacecraft's systems to their limits.
The Artemis II return process from splashdown to recovery was handled by the joint NASA-DoD team
